name: grep
when: Default line matcher. Use plain grep for portability/scripts. For interactive speed and gitignore-awareness over trees, reach for ripgrep.

name: ripgrep (rg)
when: Fastest recursive search; respects .gitignore; great defaults. First choice for searching codebases/dir trees. Has --replace for in-stream substitution.

name: the_silver_searcher (ag)
when: Predecessor to rg with similar ergonomics. Pick rg over ag for new setups; ag only if already standardized on it.

name: ack
when: Perl-based, highly portable (single script). Useful where you can't install a binary but have perl.

name: pcre2grep
when: When you specifically need full PCRE2 regex semantics that BSD/GNU grep lack (lookbehind, recursion). Otherwise rg -P covers most of this.

name: sed
when: Line-oriented substitution/deletion. BSD (mac) vs GNU sed differ on -i and regex; install gnu-sed (gsed) on mac for portability. For multiline/structured edits, prefer perl or sd.

name: sd
when: Modern find-and-replace with literal-string and sane regex syntax — no sed escaping pain. Best for straightforward s/// across files.

name: perl
when: Swiss-army for regex-heavy one-liners (-pe/-ne), multiline mode (-0777), and anything sed/awk can't express. Also a full inline language.

name: ed
when: Scriptable line editor; useful for deterministic in-place edits in constrained environments. Rarely the first choice today.

name: awk (gawk)
when: Field-based extraction and per-line compute. mac ships BSD awk; install gawk for GNU extensions. The workhorse for column math, group-by sums, reformatting.

name: frawk
when: awk-compatible but compiled/parallel — much faster on large files. Use when gawk is the bottleneck and the script is awk-expressible.

name: goawk
when: Single-binary POSIX awk with CSV mode. Handy for embedding/CI where you want awk without a system dependency.

name: cut
when: Simple byte/char/field slicing on a fixed delimiter. Fast and ubiquitous. For multi-char delimiters, regex fields, or reordering, use awk/choose/hck.

name: choose
when: cut/awk hybrid with negative indexing and ranges (e.g. choose 0 -1). Nicer ergonomics than cut for ad-hoc field picking.

name: hck
when: cut alternative with regex delimiters and field reordering, fast. Use when cut's single-char delimiter is too limiting.

name: teip
when: Masks selected fields, pipes ONLY those through another command, then splices results back. Unique: edit part of a line with an external tool without touching the rest.

name: column
when: Align columns for display (column -t). Presentation, not extraction.

name: paste
when: Merge lines side-by-side / join multiple files column-wise. Inverse-ish of cut.

name: join
when: Relational join of two SORTED files on a key. For unsorted/complex joins prefer csvq/miller/sqlite3.

name: tr
when: Translate/delete/squeeze characters. Casing, deleting char classes, squeezing whitespace.

name: rev
when: Reverse characters per line.

name: expand / unexpand
when: Convert between tabs and spaces.

name: fold / fmt / pr
when: Wrap/reflow/paginate plain text. fold = hard wrap at width; fmt = reflow paragraphs; pr = paginate with headers.

name: sort
when: Sort lines; numeric/version/key-field sort. Prerequisite for uniq and join.

name: uniq
when: Collapse/count ADJACENT duplicates — pipe sorted input. For unsorted-dedup-preserving-order use awk '!seen[$0]++'.

name: wc
when: Count lines/words/bytes/chars.

name: tac
when: Reverse line order (cat backwards).

name: shuf
when: Random permutation / sampling of lines.

name: nl
when: Number lines with formatting control (vs cat -n).

name: datamash
when: Group-by, sum/mean/median/stdev, crosstab, transpose on columnar text — without writing awk. First reach for quick stats on TSV.

name: head / tail
when: First/last N lines; tail -f to follow.

name: cat / tee
when: Concatenate / fan-out a stream to file(s) and stdout.

name: split / csplit
when: Chunk a stream/file by size, line count (split) or content pattern (csplit).

name: sponge
when: Soak up stdin fully THEN write the file — lets you 'edit in place' via a pipe (cmd file | sponge file) without truncation races.

name: pv
when: Pipe-viewer: throughput/progress bar mid-pipeline.

name: stdbuf / unbuffer
when: Force line/unbuffered I/O so streaming pipelines flush in real time. unbuffer (expect) when stdbuf doesn't take.

name: ts
when: Prefix each line with a timestamp. Quick timing/log annotation.

name: parallel (GNU parallel)
when: Run a command across many inputs concurrently with controlled jobs. More features than xargs -P (grouped output, retries, remote). For simple cases xargs suffices.

name: xargs
when: Turn stdin into args for a command. Use -0 with find -print0. For concurrency/complex output, prefer GNU parallel.

name: moreutils (suite)
when: Bundle: sponge, ts, vipe (edit a pipe in $EDITOR), vidir, ifne, chronic (run quietly unless it fails), errno, combine, pee. Install once; many show up individually above.

name: find
when: Canonical file finder with predicates/-exec. BSD vs GNU differ. For fast interactive use + gitignore, prefer fd.

name: fd
when: Fast, ergonomic find: regex by default, gitignore-aware, parallel -x. apt installs binary as fdfind. First choice interactively.

name: diff
when: Line diffs; unified/context. For word-level use wdiff/dwdiff; for prettier code diffs use delta.

name: delta
when: Syntax-highlighted pager for git/diff output. Display only — pair with diff/git.

name: wdiff / dwdiff
when: Word- or character-level diffs of prose. dwdiff lets you define delimiters.

name: patch
when: Apply a unified/context diff to files.

name: comb (comm)
when: Line-set comparison of two SORTED files (common / only-in-A / only-in-B). Set algebra, not edit diff.

name: jq
when: The standard JSON query/transform language. First choice for anything JSON. For huge streamed arrays consider jq --stream or a SQL engine.

name: gron
when: Flattens JSON to discrete grep-able assignment lines, and ungron reverses it. Use when you want to grep/sed JSON paths or diff two JSON blobs line-wise.

name: fx
when: Interactive JSON viewer/explorer (TUI) plus JS expressions. Use to explore unknown JSON; jq for scripted pipelines.

name: jo
when: BUILD JSON from shell args/values (jo name=foo n=1). The inverse of jq — construct, don't query.

name: jc
when: Parses output of ~100 commands (ls, ps, dig, ifconfig, /etc files) and many formats INTO JSON so you can pipe to jq. The bridge from unstructured CLI output to structured.

name: yq (mikefarah)
apt: # snap/go (Go version); apt 'yq' may be the python one
when: jq-syntax processor for YAML (also JSON/TOML/XML/props). Note TWO different tools named yq exist — this Go one vs a python jq-wrapper. Pin which you mean.

name: dasel
when: One selector syntax across JSON/YAML/TOML/XML/CSV — query AND convert between them. Reach for it when a pipeline crosses formats and you don't want jq+yq+xq separately.

name: taplo
when: TOML format/lint/query. Use for validating/formatting TOML; dasel or tomlq for extraction.

name: crudini
when: Get/set/del values in INI/.conf files in place. Purpose-built for INI where dasel is generic.

name: xmlstarlet
when: Full XPath/XSLT query+edit of XML. The 'jq for XML'. For quick CSS-selector scraping of HTML, prefer pup/htmlq.

name: xmllint
when: Validate/format/XPath via libxml2. Great for --format pretty-printing and schema validation; xmlstarlet for richer editing.

name: pup
when: CSS-selector extraction from HTML (like jq for HTML). First choice for scraping a page's elements.

name: htmlq
when: Same niche as pup (CSS selectors over HTML), Rust. Pick one of pup/htmlq.

name: xidel
when: XPath/CSS/XQuery over HTML+XML and can follow links/fetch. Heavier than pup; use for multi-page extraction logic.

name: html-xml-utils (hxselect)
when: Suite (hxselect/hxnormalize/...) for CSS-selecting HTML in pipelines. Alternative to pup where packaged.

name: miller (mlr)
when: awk-like but format-aware (CSV/TSV/JSON/pprint) with named fields, joins, stats, reshaping. The most general 'structured awk'. First reach for CSV transforms.

name: qsv
when: Very fast CSV toolkit (descendant of xsv) — select/join/stats/dedup/sample/index on big files. Pick qsv over xsv for new use; performance-first.

name: xsv
when: Original fast CSV swiss-army. qsv supersedes it; use xsv only if already present.

name: csvkit
when: Python suite: csvcut/csvgrep/csvjson/csvsql/in2csv (Excel→CSV!). Reach for in2csv (format ingestion) and csvsql (SQL on CSV). Slower than qsv/mlr on big data.

name: csvq
when: Run SQL directly against CSV/TSV files (SELECT/JOIN/UPDATE). Use when the transform is naturally relational.

name: dsq
when: SQL over CSV/JSON/Parquet/etc via an embedded engine. Like csvq but multi-format input. Pick one SQL-on-files tool.

name: q
when: SQL on delimited text (python). Mature but slower; sqlite3 .import or dsq often preferable now.

name: sqlite3
when: Ubiquitous SQL engine; .import CSV then query/join/aggregate, or :memory:. The dependable backbone for relational text crunching.

name: duckdb
when: Columnar analytical SQL that reads CSV/Parquet/JSON directly and FAST, even files bigger than RAM. Best modern choice for analytical queries over data files.

name: octosql
when: SQL JOINing across heterogeneous sources (CSV+JSON+postgres) in one query. Niche; duckdb covers most needs.

name: ast-grep (sg)
when: Search/lint/REWRITE source by syntax tree across many languages using code-shaped patterns. The 'jq for source code'. Use instead of regex when editing real code structure.

name: comby
when: Language-aware structural search/replace with hole patterns; good at matching balanced delimiters. Alternative to ast-grep; pick per language support.

name: srgn
when: Scope edits by language constructs (comments, strings, function bodies) via tree-sitter, then apply text ops. Use to target 'only inside strings/comments'.

name: tree-sitter (+ tsq)
when: Low-level: parse code to a queryable syntax tree. Use when ast-grep/comby/srgn don't expose what you need and you'll write tree queries.

name: pandoc
when: Universal document converter: md/html/docx/rst/latex/epub ↔ each other. First reach for any doc-format translation.

name: mq
when: jq-like query language over Markdown structure (headings/lists/code blocks). Use to extract sections programmatically rather than regexing MD.

name: glow
when: Render Markdown nicely in the terminal. Display only.

name: html2text / html2markdown
when: Strip HTML to readable text/markdown. For full doc conversion prefer pandoc; for scraping fields prefer pup.

name: lynx / w3m
when: Text browsers; -dump renders a page (incl. JS-free layout) to plain text. Good for getting article text out of HTML in a pipeline.

name: tesseract
when: Image → text OCR, many languages (install lang packs). Core OCR engine. For PDFs, wrap with ocrmypdf.

name: ocrmypdf
when: Adds a searchable text layer to scanned PDFs (uses tesseract). Use for PDF-in/PDF-out OCR; raw tesseract for images.

name: pdftotext (poppler)
when: Extract the text layer from PDFs (also pdftohtml, pdfimages, pdfinfo in poppler). Use FIRST; only OCR if there's no text layer.

name: pdfgrep
when: grep directly inside PDFs (with page numbers). Convenience over pdftotext|grep.

name: mutool (mupdf)
when: Fast PDF text/draw/extract and conversion. Alternative engine to poppler when output quality/structure differs.

name: catdoc / antiword / unrtf / docx2txt
when: Legacy office extraction: catdoc(.doc/.xls), antiword(.doc), unrtf(.rtf), docx2txt(.docx). For modern formats pandoc or libreoffice is more robust.

name: libreoffice (--headless)
when: Headless convert almost any office doc (doc/xls/ppt/odt) to pdf/txt/csv. Heavy but the most faithful office converter.

name: graphviz (dot)
when: Render DOT graph text → SVG/PNG (dot/neato/fdp/circo/twopi by layout). The standard for graph/tree diagrams from text.

name: mermaid-cli (mmdc)
when: Render Mermaid markup (flowcharts/sequence/gantt) → SVG/PNG. Uses headless Chromium (heavy). Use for Mermaid specifically; graphviz for general graphs.

name: plantuml
when: UML/sequence/component diagrams from text (needs Java + graphviz). Use for UML; graphviz/mermaid otherwise.

name: graph-easy
when: Convert between graph formats and render ASCII-art diagrams in the terminal. Unique: graph → ASCII without an image.

name: gnuplot
when: Plot numeric data → image or ASCII (set term dumb). Scriptable charts from columnar text.

name: termgraph
when: Quick bar/charts in the terminal from simple data. Lighter than gnuplot for eyeballing.

name: chafa
when: Render an image as ANSI/ASCII/sixel in the terminal. The inverse direction: image → terminal text art.

name: figlet / toilet
when: Turn a short string into large ASCII-art banners.

name: qrencode
when: Encode text/URL → QR code (PNG or terminal). zbarimg decodes the reverse.

name: whisper.cpp
when: Local audio → transcript (needs a model download). Use for offline STT; openai-whisper (python) is the heavier reference impl.

name: espeak-ng / say
when: text → speech. macOS has built-in `say`; espeak-ng is the cross-platform CLI.

name: iconv
when: Convert character encodings (e.g. latin1→utf8). For format-guessing reencode use recode.

name: recode
when: Higher-level charset/surface recoding (incl. HTML entities). iconv for plain charset, recode for entity/surface tricks.

name: dos2unix / unix2dos
when: Fix CRLF/LF line endings. Quick and purpose-built vs a tr/sed incantation.

name: base64 / base32
when: Encode/decode binary↔text. base64 -d to decode.

name: xxd / hexdump / od
when: Hex view of bytes; xxd also does the reverse (xxd -r) to rebuild binary from hex. od/hexdump are POSIX variants.

name: hexyl
when: Colored, readable hex viewer. Display nicety over xxd.

name: strings
when: Pull printable strings out of binary files.

name: envsubst
when: Substitute $VARS in a template from the environment. Simplest templating; for logic use m4/jinja.

name: m4
when: Macro processor with conditionals/includes. Powerful but arcane; reach for it for real macro expansion.

name: jinja2 (j2cli / jinja2-cli)
when: Render Jinja templates with JSON/YAML data context. Best when you have structured data + loops/conditionals.

name: python3
when: When an algorithm is given in Python, or the transform exceeds awk/jq. python3 -c for one-liners; pyp/pyped for terser stdin handling.

name: pyp
when: Python one-liner runner with implicit line/stdin vars (like perl -pe but Python). Use to avoid boilerplate for quick Python filters.

name: ruby
when: ruby -ne/-pe mirrors perl with friendlier syntax. Use when the supplied algorithm is Ruby, or you prefer it for text munging.

name: node / deno
when: JS one-liners (node -e) or running supplied JS. deno for sandboxed single-file scripts with permissions.

name: php
when: php -r / php -R for supplied PHP or its strong string functions.

name: nushell (nu)
when: A shell whose pipelines carry STRUCTURED tables, not raw text — parses CSV/JSON natively and queries them fluently. Use as the environment when you want structured pipelines end-to-end.

name: R (Rscript)
when: When the supplied algorithm is R or the task is statistical. Rscript -e for one-liners.

name: bc / dc
when: Arbitrary-precision arithmetic in pipelines. bc (infix), dc (RPN). For unit-aware math use units.

name: numfmt
when: Format numbers to/from human units (1.5K ↔ 1500). Quick humanize without awk.

name: llm
when: Simon Willison's CLI: pipe text to a model, chain prompts, run via plugins (local or API), log to SQLite. The general 'LLM step' in a pipeline. Pairs with ttok/strip-tags/files-to-prompt.

name: ttok
when: Count or truncate text by TOKENS before sending to a model. Use to fit context windows in a pipe.

name: strip-tags
when: Strip HTML to text (optionally keeping selected tags) to feed LLMs cheaply. From the same ecosystem as llm/ttok.

name: files-to-prompt
when: Concatenate a directory of files into one prompt-friendly blob (with paths). Use to feed a codebase/folder to an LLM.

name: ollama
when: Run local models; serves an API the `llm` CLI (or curl) can hit. Use for offline/local inference backing the llm step.

name: mods
when: LLM-in-a-pipe CLI from Charm with nice TUI/markdown output. Alternative to llm; pick one as the default LLM step.

name: aichat
when: All-in-one LLM CLI/REPL with sessions and RAG. Another llm/mods alternative.

name: fabric
when: Runs a library of curated prompt 'patterns' over piped input (summarize, extract_wisdom, etc.). Use for ready-made prompt recipes rather than hand-writing them.

name: aspell / hunspell
when: Spell-check text (hunspell has better dictionaries/morphology). Use -a/list mode in pipelines.

name: codespell
when: Find common misspellings in source code/comments. Tuned for code, low false positives.
